title: The Politics of AI Are About Jobs More Than Ideology
discussion_signal: The post relays evidence that partisan differences in workplace AI use largely disappear after accounting for education, occupation, and industry, while framing the remaining political divide more around exposure and displacement fears than simple ideological resistance to adoption.
linked_research_question: Are apparent partisan differences in AI adoption political preferences, or composition effects produced by where people work and what kinds of tasks they perform?
limits: Post is a researcher relay rather than a primary paper analysis
Conditioning changes the interpretation but does not eliminate all political consequences of exposure
